conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to start by asking about your child.

**First, let me ask: How old is your child (or children)?**

The age of the child is important because:
- Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (with some conditions)
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over typically don't qualify

Please tell me the age(s) of the child(ren) you're asking about.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 19 years old.

Since Alex is 19 (between 16-19 years old), they may still qualify for Child Benefit, but we need to check if they meet the education or training requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to ask about Alex's education or training status:**

Is Alex currently:
1. **In approved education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education, or approved training programs), OR
2. **Has Alex recently left education or training** (within the last few months), OR
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

This is important because Child Benefit for 16-19 year olds depends on them being in qualifying education or training, or having just left (in which case there may be a short extension period).

What is Alex's current situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is in education - he's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's helpful, thank you! Alex is studying for A-levels, which is a form of education. Now I need to verify that this qualifies under the Child Benefit rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! A-levels are specifically listed as approved non-advanced education. Now I need to check a few more details to ensure the education qualifies:

**1. Is Alex studying full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)

**2. Is this education funded by an employer or part of an agreement for a future job with an employer?**

A-levels at school or college typically count as full-time approved education, but I need to confirm these details to proceed with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying full-time at sixth form college - it's definitely more than 12 hours a week. And no, it's not funded by an employer or anything like that - it's just regular college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's great news. Alex's A-level studies at sixth form college clearly meet the approved education requirements:
- ✓ A-levels are approved non-advanced education
- ✓ Full-time (more than 12 hours per week)
- ✓ Not employer-funded

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

This is important because children aged 16 or over who work 24 hours or more per week don't qualify for Child Benefit, even if they're in education.

What is Alex's work situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex isn't working, so that requirement is satisfied.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Next question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** Specifically, is he receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

in his own name?

Children who receive these benefits in their own right don't qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex doing an apprenticeship?**

Different types of apprenticeships have different rules:
- English apprenticeships (all types) would disqualify from Child Benefit
- Scottish Modern Apprenticeships would disqualify
- Welsh Foundation Apprenticeships are approved
- Other Welsh apprenticeships would disqualify

You mentioned Alex is doing A-levels at sixth form college, so I assume he's not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not doing an apprenticeship - just his A-levels at college like I said.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not doing an apprenticeship, so that's fine.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status as the claimant. 

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

This is one of the key requirements for claiming Child Benefit. There are several ways to meet the residency requirements:
- Normally living in the UK, OR
- Having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, OR
- Having pre-settled status with certain conditions (working, job seeking, studying, etc.), OR
- Being a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries

What is your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK (in Manchester), so you meet the residency requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. You meet this requirement if ANY of the following apply:

1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care - things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents), OR
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement

**Do you live with Alex, or do you contribute to his upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you meet the responsibility requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is anyone else (like another family member) claiming for him?

What is the situation regarding other claimants for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex:**
1. **In hospital** (receiving medical care as an inpatient)?
2. **In care** (looked after by the local authority)?
3. **Fostered** (living with foster carers)?
4. **Living normally** at home with you?

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex is living at home with you normally, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is just living normally at home with me - nothing complicated like hospital or care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Just one final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

This would include things like the council paying for Alex's housing costs or providing financial support for his upkeep. Generally, you can't get Child Benefit if the local council is paying for the child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex - we're managing everything ourselves.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

Based on the information you've provided, **you meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Why You're Eligible:

**About Alex (your qualifying child):**
- ✓ Alex is 19 years old (within the 16-19 age range)
- ✓ Alex is studying A-levels full-time at sixth form college (approved non-advanced education)
- ✓ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- ✓ Alex doesn't receive benefits in his own right
- ✓ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

**About You (the claimant):**
- ✓ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✓ You live with Alex and are responsible for him
- ✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✓ The local council isn't paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000, you may need to pay some or all of the Child Benefit back through a tax charge
5. **Payments** are typically made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can start your claim here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

**Important note:** Child Benefit for 16-19 year olds continues only while they remain in approved education or training. If Alex finishes his A-levels or leaves education, you'll need to notify HMRC, as eligibility may change.

Do you have any questions about applying or anything else?
